findings.issue: AttentionItem.AssigneeAr is hard-coded null for every PhoneExpense row (ReadAllAsync, the «Phone expenses awaiting confirmation» block, ~lines 430-449). W08's «مصروفات الهاتف بانتظار التأكيد» table leads with a «الموظف» column (the mockup shows «محمد عوض» / «رنا حمدان» beside «الصالات دولية — مناقصة الطريق» and «رصيد شحن — هاتف المكتب الأرضي»), so the first column of that list renders blank for every row. This is the exact defect class fixed in round 3 for PartyAr on commitments and cases, and it survives on the one bucket the service owns end-to-end. The data IS reachable: PhoneExpense.PhoneDeviceId is a non-nullable FK into devices, and Device.EmployeeName (src/Wakeel.Core/Data/Entities/Identity.cs:92) carries the name. A screen that has to re-query per row to fill the column defeats the «one pass» contract GetAllAsync documents.
findings.fix: Mirror FillPartyNamesAsync exactly. (1) Add `e.PhoneDeviceId` to the phone-expense projection. (2) Add a second `HashSet<Guid> deviceIds` + `List<(int Index, Guid DeviceId)> devicePlaceholders` alongside partyIds/partyPlaceholders, and a local `RememberDevice(Guid id)` called immediately after each `items.Add(...)` in the expense loop (index = items.Count - 1). (3) Add `FillEmployeeNamesAsync(items, deviceIds, devicePlaceholders, ct)` next to FillPartyNamesAsync: `db.Devices.AsNoTracking().Where(d => ids.Contains(d.Id)).Select(d => new { d.Id, d.EmployeeName }).ToDictionaryAsync(...)`, then `items[i] = items[i] with { AssigneeAr = name }` when the name is non-blank (a vanished or unnamed device keeps null, like a vanished party). (4) Call it beside FillPartyNamesAsync before the `return items`. Add a test in AttentionServiceTests, e.g. APendingPhoneExpense_CarriesTheNameOfTheEmployeeWhoseDeviceSentIt, seeding two devices with distinct EmployeeName values (DailyShellWorld.EnsureDevice already creates them) and asserting each pending row's AssigneeAr. Re-run the 10k performance test — the extra query is one dictionary lookup like the party one, which cost 0 ms.

findings.issue: The database card omits «آخر فحص». The B2 spec's database row reads «قاعدة البيانات (سلامة PRAGMA integrity_check، الحجم، آخر فحص، آخر نسخة احتياطية)» and the W12 mockup's database card carries two lines («فحص السلامة: سليم» and «نسخة احتياطية أمس 23:00»). CheckDatabaseAsync (line ~368) emits only CoreAr.HealthDatabaseOk(size) — «سليمة — الحجم 2.4 غيغابايت» — with no indication of when the integrity check last ran. health_snapshots already records CheckedAt per component, so the previous run's instant is one query away.
findings.fix: In CheckDatabaseAsync, before building the Ok card, read the newest stored snapshot for HealthComponents.Database (`db.HealthSnapshots.AsNoTracking().Where(s => s.Component == HealthComponents.Database).OrderByDescending(s => s.CheckedAt).Select(s => (DateTime?)s.CheckedAt).FirstOrDefaultAsync`) and add a CoreAr overload `HealthDatabaseOk(string size, string lastCheckRelative) => $"سليمة — الحجم {size}؛ آخر فحص {lastCheckRelative}"`, falling back to the existing single-argument form when nothing is stored yet. Extend TheDatabaseCardPassesItsIntegrityCheckAndShowsTheSize with a second run asserting the «آخر فحص» clause appears.

findings.issue: NotificationPanel.Total is `rows.Count`, i.e. the size of the page just fetched (capped at `limit`, default 100), not the number of undismissed notifications. Its XML doc says «Notifications shown», which is accurate, but the record sits directly beside `Unread` — which IS the true global unread count only by accident (it is also counted over the page, so past 100 rows it under-reports too). A W10 screen rendering the «الكل N» tab from panel.Total would silently stop growing at 100. BadgeService.GetTabCountsAsync(BadgeScreens.Notifications) returns the correct numbers, so the hazard is a caller picking the wrong of two adjacent sources.
findings.fix: Either (a) compute both figures with real counts — `var total = await query.CountAsync(ct)` before the Take, and `var unread = await db.Notifications.CountAsync(n => n.DismissedAt == null && n.ReadAt == null, ct)` — so Total/Unread mean what the tabs mean; or (b) rename the two properties to Shown/ShownUnread and state in the XML doc that the tab badges come from IBadgeService.GetTabCountsAsync. (a) is preferable: the panel then needs no second service to render its own header. Add a test that creates limit+5 undismissed rows and asserts Total is limit+5 while the returned group rows number limit.

findings.issue: CheckSyncAsync (line ~594) measures the sync card's staleness with `AttentionService.BackupAgeInDays(newestOverall, utcNow)`. The maths is right — it is a generic "whole local days since" helper — but the name says backup, and the method's own XML remarks are written entirely about backups. A future change made for the backup card (clamping, a grace period, a different rounding) would silently move the «آخر مزامنة» threshold with no test naming the coupling.
findings.fix: Rename AttentionService.BackupAgeInDays to a neutral `internal static int LocalDaysSince(DateTime instant, DateTime utcNow, TimeZoneInfo? zone = null)`, rewrite its remarks to be about ages in general (keeping the local-day rationale), and update the four call sites (ReadBackupStateAsync, ReminderScheduler's backupAgeDays, CheckBackupAsync, CheckSyncAsync). Pure rename, no behaviour change; the existing TheBackupAge_IsTheSameEarlyInTheLocalMorningAsItIsLaterTheSameDay test follows the new name.

SECURITY. (a) No secret material reaches notifications, health cards, snapshots or the exported report. The health report carries only sizes (CoreAr.Size), file counts, relative times, an Office release name and the app version — no absolute path, no key, no hash, no exception text; HealthServiceTests.NoMessageMentionsAServerAPortTheInternetOrTheDatabaseEngine and TheSyncCard_NeverNamesAnEmployee enforce this and both pass. CheckSyncAsync projects only { Kind, LastSyncAt }, so the exported file names a device KIND, never a person — the right call for a file the user hands to whoever helps them. (b) Background timers cannot touch the shared session off-dispatcher: BackgroundPassDispatcher is REQUIRED by both IClockGuard.StartAsync and IReminderScheduler.Start (ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull, with tests asserting the refusal), the startup check itself goes through it, and ReminderSchedulerTests.APassAndAScreensQuery_ShareTheSessionSafelyWhenBothGoThroughTheShellsDispatcher drives 20 ticks against 20 concurrent screen queries through one gate. Both timers use Interlocked re-entrancy guards and a CancellationTokenSource torn down inside the lock, and ClockGuardTests captures the token each pass received to prove Stop cancels the in-flight pass and a second Start cancels the first binding while leaving exactly one live timer. (c) The clock guard cannot be bypassed silently: NumberingBlocked is derived from the verdict alone and is explicitly unaffected by DismissForSession (tested), EnsureNumberingAllowed throws, and OfficialNumberService refuses independently on any non-Ok verdict (IssueCoreAsync line 165) — so a caller that skips the guard is still refused. «تجاهل مؤقتًا» is an in-memory flag only, cleared by a clean check and re-raised by an Import, all three tested.

CONSUMABILITY BY THE B2 SCREENS. The interfaces are directly renderable: AttentionSnapshot hands W08 its four KPI counts, the ordered worklist, today's meetings (id/title/start/duration/location), SyncState and BackupState with ready Arabic sentences; every AttentionItem carries Kind + Id for navigation, KindLabelAr for the type chip, NumberAr/DueAt/DaysLate/NextStepAr for the W09 columns, and documents the bdi/isolate obligation on its numeric fields. Money.Shekels produces «₪ 42.50», matching the W08 mockup's phone-expense rows exactly. BadgeSnapshot.For(key) resolves item, group and bell keys from one call. ArabicRelativeTime is InvariantCulture throughout, so digits are always western (بند 20) even under an Arabic thread culture. The one gap is the medium finding: W08's «الموظف» column has no value to bind to. W08's own list tabs (الكل/مراسلات/مهام/التزامات, badged in the mockup) are not in GetTabCountsAsync, but they are derivable in memory from NeedsActionToday's Kind — that is fine and deliberate, not a gap.

TESTS. Real behaviour, no tautologies: thresholds are moved and rows are asserted to migrate between buckets (RaisingTheNearThreshold_MovesARowFromNothingIntoNear, RaisingTheStaleThreshold_TakesARowOutOfStale); the double-count rule is proved by construction (GroupBadge_CountsEachRecordOnce_EvenWhenSeveralItemsClaimIt asserts the union is strictly less than the sum); بند 56 is covered for the default, a per-meeting override, a changed default, a 2880-minute lead and a disabled reminder; بند 52's daily repetition is walked day by day until issue; idempotency is proved both by re-running a pass and by dismissing a reminder first; the sweep test proves an old UNDISMISSED row survives and only the old dismissed one is dropped; the clock-guard tests actually issue an official number and assert both the refusal and the Sequence == 1 after correction. Arabic assertions compare against the literal sentences, not against the constants they came from.

ARABIC / RTL. All user-facing Core text is Arabic with no codes and no jargon; «ويندوز» in HealthClockBad matches the W11 spec line, and «قاعدة البيانات» / «Word» match the W12 mockup's own card titles (the implementation is in fact stricter than the mockup, which prints «SQLCipher» on the database card and a raw «v3.2» on the models card — neither appears in the code). Plural agreement is handled for days, files, minutes, hours and problem counts. Core emits no markup, so bdi/isolate and icon-button tooltips remain the screen package's obligation; the records document where isolation is required.
